The Compliance Operations Analyst is responsible for supporting Liviniti ’s compliance operations, claim compliance, internal operation audits, and operational oversight functions through audit testing, claims review, data analysis, documentation, reporting, and remediation tracking.

This role assists the Manager of Compliance Operations in evaluating operational accuracy, contractual compliance, regulatory adherence, internal controls, claims processing accuracy, pricing validation, delegated vendor oversight, and fraud, waste, and abuse monitoring activities.

The Compliance Operations Analyst will help execute audit procedures, analyze claims and operational data, document findings, support corrective action follow-up, and contribute to continuous monitoring efforts that strengthen Liviniti ’s compliance posture and operational controls.

The Compliance Operations Analyst is required to perform, but is not limited to, the following responsibilities:
Audit Execution and Claims Review
Own assigned SOC audit activities, including coordination of audit requests, evidence collection, documentation review, status tracking, and follow-up with internal business owners.
Support internal audits related to claims accuracy, pass-through pricing validation, accumulator and benefit setup, claims adjudication, and operational compliance.
Perform claims sampling, testing, and validation in accordance with established audit methodologies, workplans, and review procedures.
Review claims data, system outputs, supporting documentation, SOC control evidence, and operational records to identify discrepancies, trends, or potential control gaps.
Assist with the preparation and maintenance of audit work papers, testing results, evidence files, SOC audit documentation, and supporting materials.
Track SOC audit requests, open items, remediation needs, and management responses to ensure timely completion and audit readiness.
Escalate potential findings, exceptions, control gaps, or risks to the Manager of Compliance Operations for review and direction.
Regulatory and Contractual Compliance Testing
Support testing activities designed to validate adherence to internal policies, regulatory requirements, client contractual obligations, and performance guarantee requirements.
Assist with reviews involving HIPAA/HITECH, ERISA, state PBM transparency requirements, and other applicable compliance obligations as directed.
Compare operational practices, system configurations, and claims outcomes against documented requirements and approved procedures.
Help identify areas where additional review, documentation, corrective action, or process improvement may be needed.
Maintain awareness of assigned regulatory or contractual requirements that impact claims operations, audit scope, and compliance testing
Delegated Vendor Oversight and FWA Support
Assist with delegated vendor audits, third-party oversight reviews, and service-level agreement validation.
Review delegated vendor documentation, performance data, claims activity, and supporting evidence as part of assigned audit procedures.
Support fraud, waste, and abuse review activities by analyzing utilization patterns, claim trends, provider/pharmacy activity, and other data indicators.
Document potential FWA concerns or unusual trends and escalate findings for further review.
Assist with follow-up requests, evidence collection, and tracking related to vendor or FWA review activities.
Reporting, Remediation, and Corrective Action Tracking
Assist in drafting audit summaries, issue logs, testing results, and finding narratives.
Support the development of audit reports that identify observations, findings, risk levels, root causes, and recommended corrective actions.
Maintain remediation trackers and follow up with business owners on assigned corrective and preventative action items.
Validate completion of corrective actions by reviewing supporting documentation and performing follow-up testing as needed.
Prepare status updates, dashboards, and summary materials for review by the Manager of Compliance Operations.
SOP, Governance, and Process Support
Support the development, review, and maintenance of SOPs, work instructions, process documentation, and compliance procedures.
Assist with governance workflows related to audit execution, issue tracking, evidence management, and operational compliance monitoring.
Help organize and maintain audit inventories, documentation repositories, trackers, and supporting files.

Participate in process improvement initiatives that strengthen operational controls and compliance oversight.

Assist with the creation and maintenance of audit dashboards, trackers, reports, and monitoring tools.
Review claims and operational data to identify trends, anomalies, potential compliance risks, or areas requiring additional review.
Support automated sampling, exception reporting, and continuous monitoring efforts in partnership with the Manager of Compliance Operations and Technology teams.

Revenue Operations Manager
📍 Manchester, UK (Hybrid 2 days WFH) | 💰 Up to £70,000
Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everyone by elevating UK estate agencies through world-class technology.
Your job is to own the numbers for the entire commercial engine. Not hit them, own them. You'll build the single version of the truth that runs our marketing, sales and customer success functions, and put a reliable set of numbers in front of our leadership team and board.
You will take accountability for the integrity of the full commercial funnel from top-of-funnel marketing through to churn and renewals. Right now, each function applies its own definitions and rules. You'll set one consistent set of rules and make them stick across the entire business. You'll also be responsible for forecasting, headcount planning and supporting the design of commission structures.
This is a hands-on, senior operator role. You'll own the tech stack (HubSpot sits at the centre), and you'll build the workflows, automations and permissions that keep data clean at source. You're not tidying records by hand; you're designing systems. You'll also be working with AI daily – it's not optional here. We use Claude, and you'll need to show evidence of AI already embedded in how you work.
There are no commissions or bonuses in this role and that is deliberate. The role has to stay objective about what the figures say. We've positioned the salary to reflect both your seniority and the independence you'll need to challenge senior leaders professionally and diplomatically when the numbers don't match the narrative.

s.h: HERE'S WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT TO BE WORKING ON
s.t:
Building and maintaining complete visibility across the entire revenue line: marketing pipeline, sales pipeline, churn and renewals, and capacity planning.
Setting and enforcing a single set of definitions and rules across marketing, sales and customer success, then making them stick.
Owning HubSpot end-to-end: permissions, day-to-day usage, workflow build, automations and the processes that keep data clean at source.
Producing forecasts, headcount plans and reporting that the leadership team can actually rely on.
Contributing to the design of commission plans and commercial structures.
Supporting the hiring and onboarding of a Sales Operations person, and training them to maintain what you've built.
Presenting to the board, with numbers that are clean, consistent and defensible.
Using AI to solve problems that would otherwise drown you in manual work.
Joining up the revenue line with the wider business (think product, finance, and marketing) so everybody's working from the same playbook.

You've owned reporting across a full commercial funnel (not just the sales pipeline). You can point to a forecast you owned, a commission plan you shaped and workflows you built yourself.
HubSpot is second nature to you. You operate at expert or power-user level and you can configure permissions, automations and processes without breaking into a sweat.
You've worked in multi-product SaaS at a senior level and you understand how different product lines affect pipeline, ARR and churn.
AI is already woven into how you work. You can give concrete examples of which tools you use, what you've built with them, and how they've changed your process significantly.
You can challenge senior leaders diplomatically but firmly, and you're not afraid to report the numbers as they actually are, not as people hope they'll be.
You work best with autonomy. You're a self-starter who gets the work done yourself, not someone who needs to manage others to feel productive.
You'd rather build something new than inherit a legacy system, and you're excited by the chance to define how commercial operations should work.

You've spent your career managing the sales pipeline in isolation, without visibility into marketing and customer success.
You'd struggle with HubSpot or you'd need somebody else to handle the tech stack. This is not negotiable, unfortunately.
You need variable pay to feel motivated. Commission and bonus structures feel essential to you.
AI feels like a threat rather than a tool. You see it as something that reduces your value, not something that multiplies what you can deliver.
You need a large team beneath you from day one. This role starts solo and hands-on, though you'll build a team over time.
You'd rather build strategy than do the work. The first six months are about delivery—designing the systems, building the reports, making it stick—not sitting in planning meetings.

Experience
You've spent time in a revenue operations, commercial operations or similar role, with demonstrable ownership of the full commercial funnel. You've done the work yourself – like configuring HubSpot, building forecasts, and leading alignment conversations across functions. Multi-product SaaS experience is non-negotiable; B2B exposure is strongly preferred.
Tooling
HubSpot sits at the centre, and you're an expert here. Experience with other platforms, such as Salesforce or Pipedrive, is a plus (some skills transfer). You're comfortable across other tech stacks and you use AI regularly as part of your workflow. Other tools in the stack will change and you're flexible on that front.
Communication
You can present to senior audiences without losing clarity. You push back on senior leaders when the numbers don't match the narrative, and you do it diplomatically enough that they listen rather than push back harder. You explain complex commercial logic in plain language.
Research
You think operationally. You diagnose what's broken in a process, you ask tough questions about data quality, and you can identify which problems to tackle first based on commercial impact. You're curious about how the business actually works, not just the metrics.

We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented Operations Coordinator to own the job pipeline from intake through invoice — tracking every active job, driving progress at each stage, and making sure nothing sits without action. This role is the operational engine that keeps jobs moving, keeps the team informed, and keeps the insurance process on track.
A significant portion of this role involves direct communication with insurance companies — calling adjusters, following up on claims, tracking appraisal status, and pushing for updates that allow the team to move forward. This is not a passive role. You flag stalled jobs, escalate when needed, and take initiative to get answers without being asked. If you are organized, persistent, and comfortable on the phone with insurance representatives, this role is built for you.
How the Job Pipeline Works
Understanding the full workflow is essential to succeeding in this role:
A new job comes in — you verify it meets the intake requirements and track it in the system
You ping the sales representative to confirm the inspection date has been set
Once the inspection date is confirmed, the job moves to the next stage and a claim number is assigned
You monitor all active jobs — if a job has been sitting without progress for too long, you bring it to the Operations Manager's attention immediately
You contact the insurance company by phone and email to obtain required claim documents, following up weekly until received
Field technicians go out, take photos, and capture data — that data is entered into the platform to generate the inspection report
You use the report to write the estimate and submit it to the insurance company
Once submitted, you follow up with the insurance company on the appraisal status — calling and emailing until you have an update
You communicate appraisal updates clearly to the internal team
Once approved, the information is sent to invoicing and the job moves forward to completion

Job Intake & Pipeline Tracking
Receive and log incoming jobs, verifying they meet the required criteria before moving them into the active pipeline
Track all active jobs through each stage of the process — from intake through inspection, claim submission, appraisal, and invoice
Maintain an accurate, up-to-date job tracker so the team always knows exactly where each job stands
Proactively identify jobs that have stalled or been sitting without progress and escalate them to the Operations Manager before delays become problems
Sales Team Coordination
Ping sales representatives to confirm inspection dates have been scheduled for new incoming jobs
Follow up consistently until confirmation is received — do not wait for the information to come to you
Move jobs through the pipeline stages as milestones are hit and document each transition
Insurance Company Communication — High Volume
This is one of the most critical and time-intensive parts of the role.
Contact insurance companies by phone and email to request and obtain claim documents, adjuster assignments, and claim numbers
Follow up with insurance representatives weekly — or more frequently when deadlines are approaching — until all required documents and approvals are received
Track the status of submitted estimates and appraisals, calling the insurance company to check on progress and push for updates
Communicate clearly and professionally with adjusters — you know how to be persistent without being difficult
Document all insurance communications including contact names, dates, outcomes, and promised follow-up timelines
Inspection Report & Estimate Support
Coordinate with field technicians to ensure photo and data capture from job sites is submitted in a timely manner
Enter field data into the platform to generate the inspection report
Use the completed inspection report to write the estimate and prepare it for submission to the insurance company
Ensure all estimate submissions are complete, accurate, and sent to the correct insurance contact
Appraisal Process Management
Track all submitted estimates through the appraisal process — logging submission dates and expected response windows
Follow up with the insurance company on the status of submitted appraisals — making calls to confirm receipt, ask for timelines, and request updates
Provide clear, timely appraisal status updates to the internal team so everyone knows where each job stands
Once appraisal decisions are received, communicate the outcome and relevant details to the operations and invoicing team so the job can move forward
Invoicing Handoff
Upon appraisal approval, compile and send the required information to the invoicing team
Ensure all documentation needed to close the job is organized, complete, and transmitted without delay

Prior experience in operations coordination, claims coordination, or a similar role in construction, restoration, roofing, or insurance-related services
Comfortable making a high volume of outbound calls to insurance companies, adjusters, and internal team members
Persistent and proactive by nature — you follow up without being asked and escalate before things become urgent
Highly organized with the ability to track multiple active jobs at different stages simultaneously without losing detail
Strong written and verbal communication skills — your phone calls are professional and your documentation is clear
Reliable in a remote environment with a quiet workspace and high-speed internet

Experience working with insurance claims, adjusters, or the property damage restoration process
Familiarity with construction or restoration job management platforms and reporting tools
Background in roofing, storm damage restoration, or property insurance claims coordination
Experience writing estimates or supporting the estimating process in a construction or restoration context
What Makes You a Great Fit
You look at the job tracker every morning and immediately know what needs to move today — without anyone telling you
Insurance companies hear from you on a regular, consistent schedule — not whenever you happen to remember
No job sits in your pipeline without a status, a next action, and a follow-up date
You escalate stalled jobs before the Operations Manager has to ask about them
You are the reason jobs move forward — the team counts on you to keep the pipeline flowing from the first call to the final invoice

The North America Revenue Strategy & Operations team is the operational engine behind Celonis’s go-to-market success in our highest-potential market.

This role sits on the Revenue Strategy & Operations team as a dedicated business partner to North America Sales leadership — embedding with Regional Vice Presidents and their teams to bring operational rigor, clean data, and a steady cadence to how the field runs.

Based in our Raleigh hub, you are the Strategy & Operations business partner to a portfolio of North America Sales leaders — three Regional Vice Presidents (RVPs) plus at least one adjacent GTM leader — and their teams. You’ll operate alongside a peer Strategy & Operations Manager, splitting coverage of the six-RVP NAM Sales leadership team between you so that every leader has a dedicated operator in their corner.
It’s a hands-on, high-impact role: you own the forecast and pipeline cadence for your leaders, turn scattered inputs into a clear and reliable operating picture, and sit shoulder-to-shoulder with RVPs, Sales Directors (SD), and VP+ leaders every week.

You’ll be mentored by senior operations leaders as you take ownership, and you’ll help the function get smarter over time by leveraging AI GTM capabilities to make recurring work faster, more scalable, and simpler for the field Account Executives (AEs) — unlocking real productivity gains.
The work you’ll do
Be the business partner: Serve as the dedicated Strategy & Operations partner to your portfolio of NAM Sales leaders — and their teams.
Own the forecast and pipeline cadence: Run the weekly forecast, pipeline inspection, and deal-review rhythm with your leaders; ensure roll-ups are accurate, risk-adjusted, and decision-ready for RVP and VP+ reviews.

Prepare leadership reporting and QBRs: Build the recurring reporting packages, scorecards, and QBR narratives your leaders rely on, pulling structured data from Salesforce and internal tools into decision-ready outputs.
Operate AI-native: Leverage AI GTM capabilities and agentic workflows to automate recurring reporting, accelerate deal and pipeline inspection, and make common analytical asks self-serve — simplifying how the field works and unlocking productivity.
Lead strategic initiatives: Partner on and help lead select strategic initiatives and planning workstreams for your coverage area, from framing the problem through execution and measured outcomes.

Make the function better as you go: Spot friction in how the team operates, turn manual and repetitive work into documented, repeatable systems, and continuously improve the operating rhythm.

## Your Purpose ##
Here at MSC Cruises we are looking for a Public Health Operations Manager to drive and oversee the public health operations in Brazil for MSC Cruises and Explora Journeys, acting as the key strategic partner to Brazil-s National Health Surveillance Agency (ANVISA) and other government health authorities.
You will champion regulatory excellence by ensuring full compliance with national public health requirements while enabling safe, efficient, and uninterrupted vessel operations.

The Public Health Operations Manager will also lead the design and delivery of impactful seasonal training programs, strengthen high-value relationships across local and federal health networks, and proactively influence public health initiatives that support operational success, exceptional guest experiences, and the continued growth of the business in the Brazilian market.

Public Health Operations & Compliance
* Ensure full compliance with Brazilian public health regulations across all relevant operations, including vessels calling at Brazilian ports.
* Monitor and ensure compliance with sanitation, epidemiological surveillance, potable water safety, food safety, pest control, and waste management standards.
* Coordinate inspections and audits with ANVISA and other Brazilian health authorities.
* Maintain and verify documentation required for vessel entry into Brazilian ports
Policy Monitoring, Development & Strategic Planning
* Stay up to date with changes in ANVISA regulations, policies, and inspection protocols.
* Communicate updates to relevant stakeholders and ensure operational alignment.
* Draft and update public health policies and SOPs for Brazilian operations, incorporating ANVISA requirements aligned with ANVISA-s Guide nº 65/2023 and other relevant legislation, in addition to international best practices (e.g., CDC VSP, SHIPSAN).
* Update outbreak response plans as needed for MSC / Explora Journeys and coordinate with onboard medical teams during public health events.
Liaison & Stakeholder Engagement
* Serve as the primary contact for ANVISA for both cruise brands, facilitating communication, inspections, and reporting.
* Represent Explora Journeys and MSC Cruises in regulatory meetings, industry forums, and collaborative initiatives with Brazilian health authorities.
* Build strong relationships with port health officials, local service providers, and internal stakeholders.
Training & Capacity Building
* Provide training and guidance to shipboard and shoreside teams on Brazilian public health standards.
* Support onboarding and continuous education for Public Health Officers and medical staff operating in Brazilian waters.
* Guide and support vessels in preparing for ANVISA inspections, including documentation, procedural readiness, and crew awareness.
Response Management
* Prepare and deliver timely, accurate responses to ANVISA queries and communications.
* Collaborate closely with the UK Public Health Team and MSC Brazil Legal Team to ensure responses are aligned, well-supported, and strategically delivered.
* Review and challenge ANVISA infraction notices where appropriate, ensuring a coordinated and evidence-based approach.
Internal Audit Programme
* Collaborate with MSCCM Public Health and Food Safety stakeholders to develop and implement an internal audit program aligned with ANVISA standards to proactively identify and address compliance gaps.
## Your Journey so far ##
* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Public Health or a related field.
* Proven track record in regulatory affairs, public health compliance, or maritime health operations.
* Professional experience working within or in close collaboration with ANVISA is strongly preferred.
* Deep understanding of ANVISA regulations and inspection procedures.
* Familiarity with international public health standards (USPH, SHIPSAN, ANVISA, WHO).
* Experience in outbreak investigation and response planning.
* In-depth knowledge of ANVISA regulations and Brazilian health legislation.
* Experience liaising with government agencies and drafting regulatory policy.
* Strong analytical, communication, negotiation and leadership skills.
* Ability to work cross-functionally with international teams.
* Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and other web-based collaboration tools (e.g., SharePoint, Teams).
* Fluent in Portuguese & English (written and spoken).
## Your Essentials ##
* Translating technical information into accessible language.
* Strong written and verbal communication.
* Long-term vision for public health policies and operations.
* Data-driven and impact-oriented decision-making.
* Prioritization in complex environments.

Our commitment extends to taking meaningful, measurable actions that have a long-term positive impact on our guests, our employees and our planet.

About Betterment
Betterment is a leading, technology-driven financial services company that offers investing, savings and retirement solutions for retail investors and investment advisors as well as financial wellness solutions, including a 401(k) for small and medium-sized businesses.

Our team is passionate about our mission, to empower people to build wealth with confidence and ease. We’re headquartered in NYC and offer hybrid NY-based positions (four days/ week in-office, with no required office days during the summer and winter holidays).

We're hiring an analyst and builder for our Revenue Operations team to be a force multiplier for our go-to-market organization. Sometimes that means tackling a question with no playbook yet. Sometimes it means running an established process and improving it as you go.
You'll take on ambiguous, high impact questions and turn them into clearly defined problems, design the right solution, and drive it through build, adoption, and continuous improvement.
The role has three modes. First, you'll drive the analytical core: forecasting, executive reporting, revenue planning, QBR-grade analyses over large datasets, quota and target analytics, and the models that support forecasting and planning. You'll present your own work directly to leadership and translate complex business questions into actionable insights.
Second, you'll build net-new systems: internal tools, data models, and reporting infrastructure that teammates then run and scale. That includes planning models, dashboards, and operational workflows that make the business more efficient over time.
Third, you'll make Revenue Operations more leveraged with AI, whether that's building AI-assisted tooling, designing account scoring and research logic in our go-to-market stack, or automating work that shouldn't be manual. You’ll constantly look for more opportunities to increase leverage across the organization.
The ideal candidate combines strong analytical horsepower with a systems mindset and genuine comfort with ambiguity. You ask why until you understand the business objective behind a request, you design solutions that scale beyond the first use case, and you already use AI to build and move faster than your job title suggests.

You’re naturally curious about how AI can improve the way work gets done, but you know technology is only valuable when it solves a real business problem. And you finish: to you, work is done when it's adopted, documented, and running without you, not when the analysis is shipped.
This role is based out of our NYC office.

About Seqana**
Seqana builds digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of soil carbon. We combine satellite imagery, an extensive proprietary library of soil data, and machine learning to make soil carbon measurement accurate, cost-effective, and scalable.
Regenerative agriculture can store carbon in soils while improving soil health, water quality, food security, and biodiversity. Measuring that impact is often costly and complex. Our tools help project developers, agrifood companies, NGOs, and governments credibly quantify and report the results of regenerative agricultural practices.
We’re based in Berlin, backed by venture capital investors, and supported by public funding from ESA and DLR.
Aufgaben

Operations**

Coordinate payroll with our tax firm and employer of record (EOR) provider, and own the travel expense process.
Coordinate German employment contracts and amendments, visa and immigration cases, and work with our lawyer to move them forward.

About Wayflyer
Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
The challenge
We assess businesses in minutes and send funds in as little as 24 hours. That only works if the systems behind it are fast, reliable, and built to scale as we push into new markets. Right now, that means untangling recurring problems across Underwriting, Product, and Sales, and building the automations that stop them coming back.
What you'll actually do
Root-cause the recurring problems that slow us down. You'll define your own KPIs, dig into self-sourced data, and take your findings straight to Director and VP-level leadership.
Build automations that solve a whole business domain, not a single ticket. You'll work across Jira, Hubspot, Pipedream, Tines, and Scriptrunner, and you'll own them end to end: scoping, building, testing, launching.
Run cross-functional projects from definition to delivery. You'll own the relationship with teams like Underwriting, Product & Engineering, and Sales globally, and manage dependencies that sit outside your own team.
Find the inefficiencies that span two or more business units before anyone asks you to. You'll help shape the team's roadmap and support teammates as they grow.
Build the AI layer on top of our existing workflows. Using tools like Claude and Tines' AI Agent actions, you'll build them to triage and resolve tickets, speed up routing, and add an intelligence layer on top of existing workflows, extending efforts like our ticket-scoping assistant and fraud-detection agents, not just tinkering alongside them.
What this role could turn into
This function moves people fast. Recent paths from this seat include a Senior Operations Manager role owning a full domain end to end, a Product Ops or Automation Lead role going deeper on the technical build, or a cross-functional leadership role managing a small team of Ops generalists.
Who thrives here
Someone who digs in when something breaks instead of escalating and waiting. You've done your own homework before you ask for help, and when you do ask, you bring options, not just the question. You're relentless about root cause, not just the symptom in front of you. You're sharp on prioritisation.

You know the difference between busy and useful, and you can explain why you said yes, no, or not yet in a way people accept. People also just like working with you. You're generous with your time and knowledge, and people are generous back. You care about diversity, equality, and inclusion, and you say something when we can do better.
We hire for range
You have 4+ years of relevant experience, ideally at a fast-paced start-up or scale-up, and you've owned projects independently end to end.

You can point to real examples of scoping, building, and owning workflow automations end-to-end (Jira, HubSpot, Pipedream, Tines, Scriptrunner or similar), not just supporting them, and of leading cross-functional teams to deliver solutions, including managing stakeholders outside your own team.

Hands-on SQL experience is required, along with knowledge of Python or another scripting language. You've applied AI tools like Claude or Cursor to go from idea to working code or automation, this is a requirement and we do it on a daily basis.

We care more about the trajectory you're on, though experience in financial services, fintech, or B2B is particularly interesting to us.
Location and working policy
📍 Dublin - hybrid (3 days per week in the office)
The good stuff
25 days off, plus public holidays. Private healthcare, life insurance, and a pension. Equity - because you should own a piece of what you're building. Generous parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers. 60 days a year to work abroad from wherever you want.

Execute the day-to-day work behind Gusto's Nacha, unclaimed property, and bank compliance programs, and Payment Ops' portion of SOC 1 audits. Financial Services Compliance and Payroll Compliance own these programs; you're the operational partner who keeps documentation, controls, and evidence current and coordinates with them and GRC when new requirements land.
Drive incident response for payment operations
When something breaks at scale, whether it's a failed batch, a reconciliation break, or a payment partner outage, you're in the investigation yourself, not just directing it. You keep stakeholders informed and drive the retro that prevents it from happening again.
Partner with Product and Engineering
Bring the team's operational insight into product and engineering conversations. Flag risk early, weigh in on payment-related specs, and make sure operational needs are represented, without owning the product roadmap yourself.
Lead with AI
Model and encourage the use of AI across the team, whether that's faster investigation, cleaner documentation, or automating repetitive work.

We are looking for a Chief of Staff–style operator to serve as the President’s right hand and help run, maintain, and continuously evolve the Product, Engineering & Design operating model and cadence.
This role will turn strategy into a durable execution system. You will own the connective tissue across the President’s leadership cadence: preparing the right inputs, creating clarity on decisions and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are followed through, surfacing risks early, and improving the operating model as the organization changes.

You will work across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Finance, People, and your peers in Business Operations, partnering with senior leaders who do not report to you and influencing through judgment, trust, and clarity.
The successful candidate will combine executive judgment, operational rigor, business acumen, comfort with ambiguity, strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to move fluidly between strategic questions and the execution details required to make the system work.
AI fluency is an important part of this role. You will use approved enterprise AI tools, including tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable platforms, to automate repeatable operating work, synthesize information across functions, improve leadership preparation, surface risks and dependencies, and accelerate strategic-initiative delivery.
This role reports to the VP of Operations at Squarespace and is based remotely in California or locally at our New York City headquarters.
You’ll Get To…
Run the President's operating cadence . Own end-to-end orchestration of the leadership rhythm: staff meetings, WBRs, MBRs, and QBRs, finance and portfolio reviews, priority updates, and annual operating-plan inputs. Ensure each ritual has a clear purpose, owner, input, output, decision authority, and downstream cascade.
Drive decision quality. Synthesize diverse inputs into concise narratives that make priorities, risks, options, tradeoffs, and recommended decisions clear to the President and leadership team. Document decisions in the room, assign owners and deadlines, track commitments, and escalate unresolved issues with context and a proposed path forward.
Improve execution velocity. Identify alignment and execution risks before they surface as leadership surprises, and facilitate resolution across Product, Engineering, Design, Commercial, Customer Operations, Finance, People, and Business Operations, connecting planning, performance, financial, organizational, and roadmap inputs. Use AI and advanced tooling to make decisions faster and better-informed.
Evolve the operating model. Treat the operating system as a living thing. Establish health measures such as decision latency, action closure, cascade reach, pre-read quality, participation, recurring issue themes, and use them to assess whether rituals, artifacts, and escalation paths are producing the right outcomes.

Recommend and implement changes to cadence, governance, templates, roles, and channels as strategy and priorities evolve, codifying what works so the model is easy for leaders to understand and operate.
Lead high-priority strategic initiatives. Drive complex, ambiguous, cross-functional work on behalf of the President, from framing and workplan through decision, implementation, and follow-through, including emerging problems that don't yet have a clear owner. Support annual strategy, goals, headcount, and budget processes by connecting them to the department's operating rhythm.
Represent the President and build transparency. Stand in for the President in meetings, events, and discussions, exercising the remit of the position. Navigate difficult conversations and cross-functional tradeoffs without relying on formal authority. Support two-way access to the President through Town Halls, Roundtables, Office Hours, and written follow-up, using sound judgment about what should be broadly communicated, selectively shared, or handled privately.
Serve as a trusted thought partner to the President and senior leadership team, offering an independent perspective and respectfully challenging assumptions when needed.

Significant experience in Chief of Staff, Product Operations, Business Operations, Strategy & Operations, or management consulting
A track record of owning an operating model, leadership cadence, or portfolio of complex cross-functional initiatives, preferably in tech companies
Knowledge of the product / software development lifecycle
Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise AI tools, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Glean, Cursor, or comparable approved tools, and experience integrating them into daily workflows to automate repeatable tasks, optimize processes, improve synthesis, and accelerate project delivery.
Exceptional written communication: you can turn a large volume of input into a concise, decision-ready narrative tailored to the audience
Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to understand metrics, forecasts, resource tradeoffs, product or portfolio performance, and organizational implications.
Strong executive presence and facilitation skills; you can create clarity and momentum in high-stakes or ambiguous settings.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, build consensus, resolve conflict, and push for decisions without formal authority.
High judgment and discretion when handling sensitive organizational, people, financial, and strategic information.
Comfort operating in ambiguity, switching between strategic altitude and detailed execution, and taking ownership of problems that cross organizational boundaries.
A continuous-improvement mindset: you distinguish between process and content, challenge ineffective routines, and make change practical and durable.
A bias toward action, paired with the judgment to know when to decide, when to seek input, and when to escalate.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: In the first 6–12 months, you will
s.t:
Implement a dependable operating rhythm in which leadership forums are well-prepared, decision-oriented, and followed through.
Improve the quality and consistency of pre-reads, decision logs, action tracking, portfolio updates, and quarterly communications.
Make it easy to see what changed, what matters now, what decisions are needed, who owns the next step, and where risk is accumulating.
Establish a small number of reliable AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual preparation and reporting effort, improve the timeliness and quality of leadership inputs, and make follow-through more visible.
Increase the organization’s ability to reuse knowledge, detect recurring issues, and move from raw information to clear decisions without adding unnecessary process.
Build strong working relationships and trust with the President and his leaders across the department and company, leading with tact, discretion and respect.
Help the President and leadership team make faster, clearer, better-informed decisions without adding unnecessary processes or meetings.
Leave the system more scalable and more resilient than you found it.

s.h: BUSINESS OPERATIONS ANALYST, SUPPLY CHAIN (STARLINK AVIATION)
s.t:
One of the most ambitious missions that SpaceX has undertaken to date, Starlink is leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy the world's most advanced broadband internet system and largest satellite constellation to provide fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide, connect humanity, and fund Mars colonization.

Starlink business operations combines traditional planning and analysis with broader business decision-making and strategy, directly supporting SpaceX’s leadership. Business operations is embedded in daily operations, supporting both near-term execution and long-term planning.

Team members are expected to analyze data and provide recommendations and to lead cross-functional decision-making and implementation of the recommendations. Starlink business operations is lean and dynamic, operating with a fluid structure that favors high agency.

We expect high performers to expand their scope across the program’s most critical bottlenecks.

Own global S&OP (sales & operations planning) for Starlink Aviation to convert hardware into active, happy, paying customers
Analyze key performance indicators, especially active subscribers, network utilization, produce-to-activate latency, inventory turnover, and hardware unit economics (CAC, payback period); includes developing complex S&OP models and decision-making tools
Translate analysis into strategic insights and hardware mix strategy to accelerate hardware adoption, maximize lifetime value, and minimize working capital
Orchestrate global supply allocation and demand forecasting by synthesizing complex demand signals against dynamic capacity constraints, working directly with Engineering
Drive resource planning for specific verticals, including the execution of critical hardware ramp and sunset plans in close collaboration with Hardware & Manufacturing Engineering
Enable and accelerate go-to-market execution for products post-licensing and certification to ensure zero-latency deployment
Identify initiatives for improvement of Starlink’s operational trajectory, including developing, tracking, and executing business initiatives with SpaceX’s leadership

Bachelor's degree in engineering, mathematics, computer science, data science, physics, business, or supply chain
1+ years of experience in engineering, manufacturing, product management, operations, FP&A, consulting, banking, or entrepreneurship
1+ years of experience in Excel or programming

Evidence of exceptional ability, especially within an ambiguous environment
Quantitative dual degree in engineering field and economics or business field and/or equivalent professional experience
Demonstrated success driving tangible impact/influencing within a broader organization
Extreme sense of urgency and ownership; bias toward action and automation
Ability to read and interpret income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python; ability to handle large datasets independently
Excellent analytical modeling skills (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Looker)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly with senior business leaders

Must be available to work extended hours and weekends as needed
Willingness to travel to customer sites, other SpaceX locations, and events as needed

Fraud Operations is a key function within Preply's Customer Care organisation, responsible for protecting the financial integrity of our marketplace and ensuring a safe, trusted experience for learners and tutors globally. The team operates across fraud investigations, dispute resolution, and chargeback management — partnering closely with Product, Payments, and Finance to manage risk at scale.
As Fraud Operations Manager, you will lead this team and serve as Preply's primary fraud operations authority — owning the function's strategy, operations, and people end-to-end.
What you’ll be doing
Lead, manage, and develop a team of Fraud Specialists, setting clear expectations, coaching performance, and building a high-judgement, high-accountability team culture
Own the Fraud Operations roadmap, defining priorities and aligning the function's objectives with broader business goals
Design and formalise investigation standards, workflows, escalation protocols, and documentation frameworks across the team
Define, track, and continuously improve Fraud Ops KPIs — including chargeback rate, dispute resolution SLAs, false positive rate, and financial exposure metrics
Establish a governance cadence: risk reviews, exposure reviews, and threshold calibration with Finance and senior leadership
Serve as the eyes on the ground for Product and Data — systematically translating what Specialists observe day-to-day (fraud patterns, tooling gaps, detection blind spots) into structured, actionable requirements that directly shape the detection roadmap
Cross operational observations with data to identify gaps between what is happening on the ground and what detection models are actually capturing — bringing Product and Data leads trends they can act on, not just dashboard summaries
Partner with Product, Payments, and Finance as the primary fraud authority, influencing priorities and ensuring fraud risk is embedded in key decisions
Own workforce planning and capacity management to ensure operational resilience
Present fraud performance, risk insights, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership
Drive continuous process improvement through root cause analysis, policy adherence, and tooling evolution
What you need to succeed
6-8+ years of experience in fraud operations, payments risk, or financial crime — with demonstrated people management experience
Proven track record leading fraud or risk operations in a marketplace, fintech, or e-commerce environment
Deep expertise in fraud investigation methodology, chargeback management, and fraud detection workflows
Experience owning operational KPIs and translating data into decisions and priorities
Strong people leadership: you build teams, develop talent, and create cultures of rigour and ownership
Able to translate operational observations into clear requirements for Product and Data — comfortable working with PMs and data leads as peers, not just as stakeholders to manage
Strong data fluency: you combine what you see in operations with what the data shows, identify gaps between ground-level reality and what detection is capturing, and surface actionable trends
Skilled at designing scalable processes and governance frameworks that outlast any individual
Strong understanding of how AI and machine learning models are applied in fraud detection — including how to interpret model outputs, evaluate signal quality, and partner with technical teams to drive detection improvements

Familiarity with ML-based fraud detection and feedback loop workflows
SQL or BI fluency (e.g. Looker, Tableau)
Experience in a multi-currency, cross-border marketplace environment
Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) or Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)
Experience with fraud detection platforms (e.g. Sardine, Sift, Feedzai, Kount)
